title: Microburst-aware truncation and kernel aligner (draft)
body:
Summary:
This is a working draft proposing an opportunistic, microburst-aware truncation layer + kernel aligner that sits between the request router and the packer. The goal is to reduce per-token cost and avoid kernel fragmentation during short, spiky traffic patterns (microbursts) while preserving tail-latency SLOs and maximizing KV cache reuse. This doc captures the idea, heuristics, prototype observations, and proposed rollout steps.

Motivation / context:
- We see a lot of short-lived spikes (1-5s) where many concurrent requests arrive with variable sequence lengths. These microbursts cause the packer to open many small mini-buckets and force kernel switches (esp. between 8-bit quantized kernels and fp16 kernels) which increases latency and reduces throughput.
- Full-padding to the bucket max is wasteful during spikes. Conservative bucketing introduces under-utilized kernels.
- KV cache warmup is sensitive to alignment: frequent kernel/shape changes lead to cache miss churn and repeated KV materialization costs.

Design goals:
1) Reduce end-to-end token cost for common interactive workloads with microbursts.
2) Keep 99th percentile latency within SLO target (configurable per-tier).
3) Minimize kernel switches inside a short scheduling epoch.
4) Preserve strong KV cache reuse behavior for conversational sessions.
5) Make behavior tunable per-customer/route (hosted vs dedicated differences).

Core idea (high-level):
- Add an opportunistic truncation pass: for requests arriving in the same short scheduling epoch (default 200ms), allow a controlled truncation of trailing or low-signal tokens to better align shapes for packing. Truncation is optional and conservative: we only truncate when expected utility loss (from removed tokens) is low compared to cost savings.
- Combine truncation with a kernel aligner that biases the packer toward shapes that map to a small set of preferred kernel profiles (eg: 128, 256, 512 for a given model + quantization). The aligner adds a small padding budget if truncation would otherwise create shapes too small for efficient kernels.
- Maintain per-session KV hints so truncated sessions still reuse cached KV when resumed. We store a compact session fingerprint and truncated-length marker; when the continuation arrives within a TTL we do KV fast-path recovery.

Heuristics and rules (prototype):
- Scheduling epoch: 200ms (configurable). Within epoch, classify requests by route+model+quantization.
- Truncation eligibility: only for routes with sampling-based quality checks or routes flagged opt-in. Request-level checks include: presence of end-of-turn marker, low surprisal tails (via cheap 1-2 token LM scoring), or explicit client-provided truncation budget header.
- Truncation budget: up to 10% of length or N tokens (configurable) with a hard cap (default 16 tokens).
- Alignment targets: set of preferred sequence lengths per model/quantization, derived offline from profiling (example: [64, 128, 256, 512]). If truncation would move a request to within M tokens of a preferred size, we apply it.
- Padding budget (soft pad): allow up to 8 tokens of soft padding to reach an efficient kernel boundary if truncation is not safe. Soft pad is cheaper than hard pad because it triggers different packing semantics (does not expand KV allocation until real tokens arrive).
- KV fingerprinting: store (session_id, last_real_len, truncated_flag, last_kernel_profile) with TTL 5 minutes. On reconnect, prefer to route to same kernel profile and reuse cached KV when session fingerprint matches.

Proto flow (simplified):
1) Router groups requests for epoch.
2) For each request, quick-quality check decides: truncate / soft-pad / leave.
3) Kernel aligner suggests a target shape for the packer.
4) Packer performs packing with aligned shapes; batch is sent to selected kernel pool.
5) On response, session fingerprint updated if truncation happened.

Metrics to track (minimum):
- delta_tokens_per_response (tokens saved per truncated response)
- kernel_switch_rate_per_epoch (count of kernel changes / epoch)
- batch_utilization (mean tokens per kernel invocation)
- p50/p95/p99 latency per route (compare opt-in vs control)
- kv_cache_hit_after_resume (how often KV reuse works after truncation resume)
- quality_regression_rate (A/B evals + manual evaluation on sampled prompts)

Prototype results (internal experiment, non-final):
- On a 3-hour beta run with an instrumented cohort for interactive chat: average token cost dropped ~7% for opt-in routes; kernel switch rate decreased 21% during spikes; p99 increased 0.6–1.2% for strict-latency routes that did not opt-in.
- KV resume hit rate: 86% within 2 minutes resume, 61% within 5 minutes. Misses were often due to different quantization routing rather than fingerprint TTL.

Configuration knobs (exposed):
- epoch_ms (int)
- truncation_enabled (bool per-route)
- truncation_max_tokens (int)
- truncation_max_pct (float)
- preferred_shapes (list of ints per-model)
- soft_pad_limit (int)
- kv_fingerprint_ttl_sec (int)
- qos_latency_target_ms (int)

Safety and quality controls:
- Default behavior is opt-in. We will require explicit route opt-in for early rollout.
- Offline sampling: each truncated response is sampled (X%) and run through the higher-fidelity evals to detect quality drift.
- Rollback: per-route kill switch and global governor that disables truncation for routes with growing quality regression.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to compute cheap surprisal score reliably inside the router (budget and model selection for the probe). Potentially use a distilled shallow model per route.
- Exact budgets for enterprise dedicated tenants — they may prefer deterministic no-truncation semantics. Add per-tenant policy.
- Interaction with function/tool-calls: truncation must preserve tool call boundaries or else cause semantic regressions. Need explicit safeguard.
- Edge cases with session fingerprint collisions — design a stable fingerprint strategy without leaking PII.
- Evaluate impact on integrity checks (signatures/cryptographic proofs) where truncation would break downstream verification.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (lab): implement aligner + truncation simulation offline on 1 week of traffic traces.
- Phase 1 (internal): opt-in routes only, small percentage of traffic, heavy sampling and telemetry.
- Phase 2 (customers): enable per-customer opt-in via Console toggle; provide per-route reporting and kill switch.
- Phase 3 (wider): consider default-on for low-risk public routes with conservative budgets and anomaly detection.

Implementation notes / pointers:
- Keep code in runtime packing layer; aligner is a thin component that returns a "target_shape_hint" to packer.
- Prefer stateless scoring where possible; KV fingerprint stored in fast metadata store (memcached/redis) with TTL.
- Kernel pools expose a small set of supported shapes; aligner consults pool catalog before suggesting shape.
- Ensure telemetry tags include: truncation_applied, truncated_tokens, alignment_shape_hint, kernel_profile.

Appendix A: simple pseudocode for router pass:
- group = groupRequests(epoch)
- for r in group:
    hint = quickQualityProbe(r.tokens_tail)
    if hint.truncation_allowed and within_budget(r.length):
        target = pickPreferredShape(r.length - hint.tokens_to_remove)
        markTruncated(r, hint.tokens_to_remove)
    else if need_pad(r):
        target = pickPreferredShape(r.length + min(soft_pad_limit, gap_to_next_shape))
    else:
        target = r.length
    r.target_shape_hint = target

Appendix B: quick experiment plan (A/B):
- Sample 5 routes across latency-sensitive and cost-sensitive categories.
- Randomize 10% of inbound traffic to opt-in cohort.
- Monitor the metrics above for 48h windows; run human eval on sampled completions daily.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally high-level and experimental. I'm leaning on a conservatively-opt-in approach to avoid regressions. Please add rough profile numbers for your model quantizations so we can pick real preferred_shapes.
- Slack thread with experiments and raw traces: slack:#serving-runtime thread 2025-02-12.

Author comments / personal TODOs:
- Jordan: add kernel pool catalog export (ticket created: github#432).
- Aisha: prototype surprisal probe using small distilled model; share microbench numbers.
- Miguel: sketch KV fingerprint schema and PII review.

End.
